instruction: I want to find out the bitrate of this video file. Please determine the video bitrate and save it to a file named "bitrate.txt" in /home/user/ containing just the bitrate value in kbps as an integer (e.g., "2500").

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting video bitrate using ffprobe or similar tool. Video bitrates typically range from 100 kbps (low quality) to 50000 kbps (very high quality). Evaluator validates bitrate is within reasonable range.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies file creation at the specified path (/home/user/bitrate.txt)
Metric logic correctly handles expected parameter (type='rule') - directly accesses expected.get('min_bitrate_kbps') and expected.get('max_bitrate_kbps') without incorrect patterns
Data flow is semantically correct: get_vm_file fetches file → metric reads content → parses as integer → validates range
Error handling is robust (handles None result, ValueError for parsing, general exceptions)
Coverage is complete for verifiable requirements (file existence, integer format, plausible value)
Range validation (100-50000 kbps) is semantically appropriate for typical video bitrates
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider documenting that the evaluator validates plausibility (range check) rather than absolute correctness, as the actual video bitrate is not provided as ground truth
Minor improvement: Could add more granular scoring (partial credit) if the value is close to range boundaries, though current binary pass/fail is acceptable
